conventions.convention: The heat operator is ∂t−Δx. The kernel is (4πt)^(−n/2) exp(−|x|²/(4t)) for n≥1 and t>0; its causal extension is zero for t≤0.
Heat evolution acts on almost-everywhere Lp classes, with H0 the identity. Countable Choice is assumed; strong initial convergence and mild uniqueness are stated for 1≤p<∞.
The Fourier transform uses exp(−2πix·ξ), giving the heat multiplier exp(−4π²t|ξ|²). The unnormalized transform is distinguished explicitly.

Bounded-domain traces use bounded C¹ graph domains in dimension n≥2, 1≤p<∞, real or complex scalars, surface measure, and almost-everywhere classes. Connectedness of the domain is not required. The Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Flattening places the domain below its boundary graph; the outward normal points out of that subgraph. Flat trace arguments reflect to the upper half-space, where ∂n denotes the last coordinate derivative.

The fractional norm is the Lp norm plus the Slobodeckij seminorm; the diagonal integrand is zero and integration uses completed product measure. The trace exponent θ=1−1/p is used only for 1<p<∞; no W^(0,1) endpoint space is introduced.
Boundary fractional norms use finitely many chart-localized functions extended by zero inside their support margins; atlas independence means equivalence of norms.

The Poisson example gives a global W^(1,2) lift for all smooth compactly supported data when boundary dimension d≥2; for d=1 it requires zero mean. Compact cutoff lifts give the local trace in every dimension.

Finite étale covers allow the empty cover. The fundamental group is Aut of the geometric fibre functor with its finite-fibre action topology; classification uses continuous left actions, with the opposite deck-group convention made explicit. AC is assumed.
The fpqc covering convention concerns a single flat, surjective, quasi-compact morphism, rather than an arbitrary covering family.
The empty space is connected; classification of connected covers as transitive actions explicitly requires nonempty covers.
The specialization interface uses a complete Noetherian DVR with algebraically closed residue field, not merely a separably closed residue field.

Specialization goes from the generalizing geometric fibre to the special geometric fibre. A trait, field comparisons, and compatible paths are selected; changing a path conjugates the map. In positive residue characteristic p, the prime-to-p quotient uses finite quotient groups of order prime to p.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice and n≥1. For t>0 the heat kernel is positive with unit mass, obeys Γ(λx,λ²t)=λ^(−n)Γ(x,t), is smooth and satisfies ∂tΓ=ΔxΓ, and has spatial derivative bounds C(n,α)t^(−(|α|+n)/2)exp(−|x|²/(8t)). Its L1 norm is one and the kernels form an L1 approximate identity.

Assume AC. For a commutative ring A and a module-finite commutative A-algebra D, finite presentation as an A-module is equivalent to finite presentation as an A-algebra. Consequently Spec D→Spec A is finite étale iff D is finitely presented and flat as an A-module and Ω(D/A)=0. Its underlying module is finite projective and locally free of finite rank; rank is locally constant and counts geometric fibre points. No Noetherian hypothesis on A is required.

Assume AC. On a bounded C¹ graph domain Ω⊂Rⁿ, n≥2, with chart-independent surface measure, 1≤p<∞ and real or complex scalars, there is a unique bounded linear T:W^(1,p)(Ω)→Lp(∂Ω) agreeing with restriction for every continuous Sobolev representative on the closure. It satisfies the stated norm bound and is the transported flat trace in boundary charts, with agreement on overlaps.

Assume AC. For a connected scheme X with algebraically closed geometric basepoint, its fibre functor gives an equivalence between FEt(X) and finite sets with continuous left action of π1ᵉᵗ(X). The group is profinite; connected nonempty covers correspond to transitive nonempty actions. Neither local Noetherianity nor finite type is required.

Assume AC. If R is a complete Noetherian DVR and X→Spec R is smooth and proper, restriction FEt(X)→FEt(X0) is an equivalence. Projectivity is not assumed; empty or disconnected families are allowed. No assertion is made for arbitrary singular proper total spaces.

Assume AC. For a Noetherian regular local ring (A,m) of dimension d≥2, every finite étale cover of Spec A minus its closed point extends to a finite étale cover of Spec A, uniquely up to unique compatible isomorphism. No equicharacteristic, excellence or dimension bound is imposed.

Assume AC. Let A be complete Noetherian regular local of dimension d≥3, f∈m minus m², U its punctured spectrum, and Un=U×Spec(A/fⁿA). For finite locally free sheaves E,G on U, HomU(E,G)→lim HomUn(E|Un,G|Un) is a bijection. Compatible isomorphisms, inverses and algebra-structure identities extend uniquely.
Assume AC. For a bounded C¹ domain Ω⊂Rⁿ, n≥2, 1<p<∞ and θ=1−1/p, T is bounded W^(1,p)(Ω)→W^(θ,p)(∂Ω) and onto. Its range is a strict subset of Lp(∂Ω), and T is not compact into the fractional target.
Assume AC. For a bounded C¹ domain Ω⊂Rⁿ, n≥2, and 1≤p<∞, the kernel of T on W^(1,p)(Ω) equals W0^(1,p)(Ω), the W^(1,p) closure of Cc∞(Ω).

Assume AC. For d≥1, 1<p<∞ and θ=1−1/p, the stated scale-mollification lift R+g(x,t)=η(t)(g*φt)(x) belongs to W^(1,p) of the half-space, has the displayed tangential and normal derivative formulas, satisfies the stated boundedness estimate, and obeys T+R+g=g.

Assume AC. For faithfully flat quasi-compact p:S′→S, pullback is an equivalence between finite étale S-schemes and finite étale S′-schemes with a cocycle descent isomorphism. Morphisms commute with that datum. This includes effectiveness, uniqueness up to unique compatible isomorphism, and descent of morphisms, without Noetherian hypotheses.

Assume AC. Let A be a Noetherian DVR with uniformizer t and residue characteristic p, and L/F finite Galois of order n. If p=0 or p does not divide n, the integral closure of A[θ]/(θⁿ−t) in L⊗F F(θ) is finite étale over that DVR. A common root similarly kills the stated vertical ramification in a smooth proper trait family.
